source_text: Ἄνθρωπος εἰς τρίτον ἁρπαγεὶς οὐρανὸν, καὶ εἰς παράδεισον ἀπενεχθεὶς, καὶ μυστηρίων κοινωνήσας ἀποῤῥήτων, καὶ τοσαύτης πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ἀπολαύσας παῤῥησίας, οὐ σφόδρα αἴσθησιν ἐκείνων ἐλάμβανε τῶν ἀγαθῶν, εἰ μὴ καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς εἶδε σὺν αὐτῷ διασωζομένους. Οἶδε γὰρ, οἶδε σαφῶς, ὅτι ἀγάπης οὐδὲν οὔτε μεῖζον οὔτε ἴσον ἐστὶν, οὐδὲ αὐτὸ τὸ μαρτύριον, ὃ πάντων ἐστὶ κεφάλαιον τῶν ἀγαθῶν· καὶ πῶς, ἄκουσον. Ἀγάπη μὲν γὰρ καὶ χωρὶς μαρτυρίου ποιεῖ μαθητὰς τοῦ Χριστοῦ, μαρτύριον δὲ χωρὶς ἀγάπης οὐκ ἂν ἰσχύσειε τοῦτο ἐργάσασθαι. Πόθεν τοῦτο δῆλον; Ἀπ' αὐτῶν τῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ ῥημάτων· πρὸς γὰρ τοὺς μαθητὰς ἔλεγεν· Ἐν τούτῳ γνώσονται πάντες, ὅτι μαθηταί μού ἐστε, ἐὰν ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους. Ἰδοὺ ἀγάπη χωρὶς μαρτυρίου μαθητὰς ποιεῖ. Ὅτι δὲ μαρτύριον χωρὶς ἀγάπης οὐ μόνον μαθητὰς οὐ ποιεῖ, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ὠφελεῖ τι τὸν ὑπομένοντα, ἄκουσον Παύλου λέγοντος· Ἐὰν παραδῶ τὸ σῶμά μου, ἵνα καυθήσωμαι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐδὲν ὠφελοῦμαι. βʹ. Διὰ τοῦτο μάλιστα τὸν ἅγιον τοῦτον φιλῶ τὸν σήμερον ἡμᾶς συναγαγόντα, τὸν μακάριον Ῥωμανὸν, ὅτι μετὰ τοῦ μαρτυρίου πολλὴν τὴν ἀγάπην ἐπεδείξατο, διὸ καὶ τὴν γλῶτταν ἐξεκόπτετο τὴν ἁγίαν. Καὶ γὰρ καὶ τοῦτο ἄξιον ἐξετάσαι, τί δή ποτε οὐκ ἐπὶ βασάνους καὶ κολάσεις καὶ τιμωρίας ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος, ἀλλὰ τὴν γλῶτταν ἀπέτεμεν· οὐ γὰρ εἰκῆ τοῦτο ἐποίησεν, ἀλλὰ μετὰ πολλῆς τῆς πονηρίας· καὶ γὰρ κακουργόν ἐστι τὸ θηρίον, καὶ πάντα κατὰ τῆς ἡμετέρας σωτηρίας πραγματεύεται καὶ κινεῖ. Φέρε οὖν ἐξετάσωμεν, τί δήποτε ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκοπὴν τῆς γλώττης ἐχώρησε, μικρὸν γοῦν ἀνωτέρω τὸν λόγον ἀγαγόντες· οὕτω γὰρ εἰσόμεθα καὶ τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ φιλανθρωπίαν, καὶ τὴν τοῦ μάρτυρος ὑπομονὴν, καὶ τὴν τοῦ διαβόλου κακουργίαν· καὶ τὴν μὲν τοῦ Θεοῦ φιλανθρωπίαν μαθόντες εὐχαριστήσομεν τῷ Δεσπότῃ, τὴν δὲ τοῦ μάρτυρος ὑπομονὴν γνόντες μιμησόμεθα τὸν σύνδουλον, τὴν δὲ τοῦ διαβόλου κακουργίαν καταμαθόντες, ἀποστραφησόμεθα τὸν ἐχθρόν. Διὰ γὰρ τοῦτο ἡμῖν ἔδωκεν ὁ Θεὸς εἰδέναι αὐτοῦ τὰς μηχανὰς, ἵνα μειζόνως αὐτὸν μισήσαντες εὐκολώτερον αὐτοῦ περιγενώμεθα. Ὅτι γὰρ δυνατὸν εἰδέναι αὐτοῦ τὰ νοήματα, ἄκουσον τί φησιν ὁ Παῦλος περὶ τοῦ πεπορνευκότος· Κορινθίοις γὰρ ἐπιστέλλων οὕτω πώς φησι· Κυρώσατε εἰς αὐτὸν ἀγάπην, ἵνα μὴ πλεονεκτηθῶμεν ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ· οὐ γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὰ νοήματα ἀγνοοῦμεν. Τίς οὖν ἡ αἰτία, δι' ἣν τὴν γλῶτταν ἐξέκοψε; Μικρὸν ἄνωθεν ἀνάσχεσθέ μου διηγουμένου. Πόλεμος ἀνεῤῥιπίσθη ποτὲ κατὰ τῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν χαλεπὸς, οὐχὶ βαρβάρων ἐπιδραμόντων τὰς πόλεις, οὐδὲ ἀλλογενῶν τινων, ἀλλ' αὐτῶν τῶν δοκούντων προεστάναι τῆς καθ' ἡμᾶς οἰκουμένης, καὶ βαρβάρων, καὶ πολεμίων, καὶ τυράννων ἁπάντων ἀπηνέστερον καὶ ὠμότερον κεχρημένων τοῖς ὑπηκόοις. Οὐ γὰρ ὑπὲρ ἐλευθερίας, καὶ πατρίδος, καὶ χρημάτων, καὶ τῆς παρούσης ζωῆς ὁ κίνδυνος ἦν τότε, ἀλλ' ὑπὲρ βασιλείας οὐρανῶν, καὶ τῶν ἀποκειμένων ἀγαθῶν, ὑπὲρ ἀθανάτου ζωῆς, ὑπὲρ ὁμολογίας τῆς εἰς τὸν Χριστόν. Καὶ καινός τις αἰχμαλωσίας ἐπενοεῖτο τρόπος· οὐ γὰρ τῆς ἐνταῦθα πόλεως ἐξέβαλλον, ἀλλὰ τῆς ἄνω Ἱερουσαλὴμ τῆς ἐλευθέρας ἐπεχείρουν ἀποστερεῖν, καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἕκαστον καταθύειν ἠνάγκαζον ἐπὶ τῶν βωμῶν, καὶ τὸν οἰκεῖον Δεσπότην ἐξόμνυσθαι, καὶ τῇ τῶν δαιμόνων ὑποκύπτειν τυραννίδι, καὶ τοὺς λυμεῶνας καὶ ἐχθροὺς τῆς σωτηρίας τῆς ἡμετέρας θεραπεύειν δαίμονας· ὃ μυρίων θανάτων καὶ πάσης γεέννης χαλεπώτερον ἦν καὶ ἀφορητότερον ταῖς φιλοχρίστοις ψυχαῖς.
thought_title: Love greater than martyrdom; why the devil cut out Romanus's tongue
orientation: Chrysostom is praising the martyr Romanus and now explains why love is greater even than martyrdom, then begins to ask why the devil cut out Romanus's tongue rather than killing him.
pass_a_gloss: A man caught up to the third heaven, and carried away into paradise, and having shared in secret mysteries, and having enjoyed so much boldness toward God, did not strongly take perception of those good things, unless he also saw the brothers being saved together with him. For he knew, he knew clearly, that of love nothing either greater or equal is, not even martyrdom itself, which is the chief point of all good things; and how, listen. For love even without martyrdom makes disciples of Christ, but martyrdom without love would not be able to accomplish this. From where is this clear? From the very words of Christ; for to the disciples he was saying: By this all will know, that you are my disciples, if you love one another. Behold love without martyrdom makes disciples. And that martyrdom without love not only does not make disciples, but does not even benefit the one enduring, listen to Paul saying: If I hand over my body, so that I may be burned, but do not have love, I am benefited nothing. 2. For this reason especially I love this holy one who gathered us today, the blessed Romanus, because with the martyrdom he displayed much love, for which reason also he was having cut out the holy tongue. For indeed this too is worthy to examine, why ever not to tortures and punishments and penalties did the devil lead him, but cut off the tongue; for not without purpose did he do this, but with much wickedness; for the beast is crafty, and all things against our salvation he schemes and sets in motion. Come then let us examine, why ever to the cutting out of the tongue he proceeded, having brought the word a little further up; for thus we will know both the love of God toward humanity, and the endurance of the martyr, and the wickedness of the devil; and having learned the love of God toward humanity we will give thanks to the Master, and having known the endurance of the martyr we will imitate the fellow servant, and having understood the wickedness of the devil, we will turn away from the enemy. For for this reason God gave us to know his schemes, in order that having hated him more greatly we may more easily overcome him. For that it is possible to know his thoughts, listen to what Paul says about the one who had committed fornication; for writing to the Corinthians he says something like this: Confirm toward him love, in order that we may not be taken advantage of by Satan; for we are not ignorant of his thoughts. What then is the cause, for which he cut out the tongue? Bear with me a little as I narrate from above. A war was stirred up once against the Churches, harsh, not of barbarians running upon the cities, nor of any foreigners, but of those themselves seeming to preside over the world inhabited by us, and more savage and more cruel than all barbarians and enemies and tyrants treating their subjects. For not over freedom, and fatherland, and money, and the present life was the danger then, but over the kingdom of the heavens, and the good things laid up, over immortal life, over confession toward Christ. And a new kind of captivity was being devised; for not from the city here were they casting out, but of the Jerusalem above, the free one, they were attempting to deprive, and the soul each one they were forcing to sacrifice upon the altars, and to renounce the proper Master, and to bow down to the tyranny of the demons, and to serve the destroyers and enemies of our salvation, the demons; which thing than ten thousand deaths and than all Gehenna was more grievous and more unbearable to the Christ-loving souls.

choices.term: ἀγάπης οὐδὲν οὔτε μεῖζον οὔτε ἴσον ἐστὶν
choices.english: of love nothing either greater or equal is
choices.why: Keeps the double negation and the genitive of comparison literally, preserving the rhetorical force of the superlative claim
rejected: nothing is greater than or equal to love

choices.english: would not be able to accomplish this
choices.why: The optative with ἂν expresses a potential; rendering as 'would not be able' preserves the hypothetical force
rejected: is not strong enough to do this

choices.english: so that I may be burned
choices.why: The ἵνα with subjunctive expresses purpose; the passive subjunctive is rendered literally

choices.english: he was having cut out the tongue
choices.why: The imperfect passive indicates an ongoing or repeated action in the past; the literal rendering preserves the aspect

choices.english: of the Jerusalem above, the free one
choices.why: The appositional adjective 'the free one' is kept in its source position to preserve the Pauline echo (Galatians 4:26)

choices.term: ὃ μυρίων θανάτων καὶ πάσης γεέννης χαλεπώτερον ἦν
choices.english: which thing than ten thousand deaths and than all Gehenna was more grievous
choices.why: The relative pronoun is kept as 'which thing' to preserve the source's resumptive structure, and the genitives of comparison are rendered with 'than'
rejected: which was more grievous than ten thousand deaths and all Gehenna

pass_b_english: A man caught up to the third heaven and carried away into paradise, who shared in secret mysteries and enjoyed such boldness before God, did not receive strong perception of those good things unless he also saw his brothers being saved along with him. For Paul knows—Paul knows clearly—that of love nothing is either greater or equal, not even martyrdom itself, which is the chief point of all good things. And how is this so? Listen. Love, even without martyrdom, makes disciples of Christ, but martyrdom without love would not be able to accomplish this. From where is this clear? From the very words of Christ. For he said to his disciples, “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another” (John 13:35). See, love without martyrdom makes disciples. And that martyrdom without love not only does not make disciples but does not even benefit the one enduring it, listen to Paul saying, “If I hand over my body to be burned, but do not have love, I gain nothing” (1 Corinthians 13:3).

For this reason I especially love this holy man who has gathered us here today, the blessed Romanus, because along with martyrdom he displayed great love, and for this reason his holy tongue was cut out. And indeed this too is worth examining: why ever did the devil not lead him to tortures and punishments and torments, but cut off his tongue? For he did not do this without purpose, but with great wickedness. For the beast is crafty, and he works and moves everything against our salvation. Come then, let us examine why ever he proceeded to the cutting out of the tongue, bringing the account a little further back. For in this way we will know both the love of God toward humanity, and the endurance of the martyr, and the wickedness of the devil. And when we learn the love of God toward humanity, we will give thanks to the Master; when we know the endurance of the martyr, we will imitate our fellow servant; and when we understand the wickedness of the devil, we will turn away from the enemy. For this reason God has given us to know his schemes, so that by hating him more we may overcome him more easily. And that it is possible to know his thoughts, listen to what Paul says about the man who had committed sexual immorality. For writing to the Corinthians he says something like this: “Reaffirm your love for him, so that we may not be outwitted by Satan; for we are not ignorant of his designs” (2 Corinthians 2:8, 11).

What then is the reason for which he cut out the tongue? Bear with me a little while I narrate from earlier. A harsh war was once stirred up against the Churches—not with barbarians attacking the cities, nor with any foreigners, but with those who seemed to rule over our world, who treated their subjects more savagely and more cruelly than all barbarians and enemies and tyrants. For the danger then was not for freedom and homeland and possessions and the present life, but for the kingdom of heaven and the good things stored up, for immortal life, for confession of faith in Christ. And a new kind of captivity was devised. For they did not cast people out of the city here below, but they attempted to deprive them of the Jerusalem above, the free one, and they forced each person to slaughter his own soul upon the altars, to renounce his own Master, to bow down to the tyranny of demons, and to serve the destroyers and enemies of our salvation—the demons. This was more grievous and more unbearable to Christ-loving souls than ten thousand deaths and all Gehenna.

problems.quote: he was having cut out his holy tongue
problems.source_quote: διὸ καὶ τὴν γλῶτταν ἐξεκόπτετο τὴν ἁγίαν
problems.why: Greek is imperfect passive/middle 'was having his tongue cut out,' but English 'was having cut out' is ungrammatical and obscures agency; it reads as if he arranged it himself.
problems.fix: for this reason his holy tongue was cut out

edits.old: and for this reason he was having cut out his holy tongue
edits.new: and for this reason his holy tongue was cut out

fixed: Changed 'he was having cut out his holy tongue' to 'his holy tongue was cut out' because the Greek imperfect passive/middle (ἐξεκόπτετο) describes the tongue being cut out, not the martyr arranging it; the original English was ungrammatical and obscured agency.

problems.why: Subject is Paul, not generic 'he'; needs 'Paul knows' or 'he [Paul] knows'

problems.quote: did not strongly feel those good things
problems.source_quote: οὐ σφόδρα αἴσθησιν ἐκείνων ἐλάμβανε τῶν ἀγαθῶν
problems.why: οὐ σφόδρα negates the verb; he did NOT receive strong perception of those goods.
problems.fix: did not receive strong perception of those good things
problems.ruling: οὐ σφόδρα modifies αἴσθησιν, not ἐλάμβανε: 'did not receive strong perception,' not 'strongly did not receive perception.'

edits.old: did not strongly feel those good things
edits.new: did not receive strong perception of those good things

fixed: Subject is Paul, not generic 'he'; source: Οἶδε γὰρ, οἶδε σαφῶς, referring to Paul from the preceding sentence.
οὐ σφόδρα negates the verb; source: οὐ σφόδρα αἴσθησιν ἐκείνων ἐλάμβανε τῶν ἀγαθῶν, meaning he did not receive strong perception of those good things.

problems.quote: so that I may be burned
problems.why: The Greek subjunctive καυθήσωμαι is passive "so that I may be burned," but Paul (1 Cor 13:3) says "if I hand over my body to be burned"—the English "so that I may be burned" suggests voluntary self-immolation rather than surrendering to be burned by others.

edits.old: so that I may be burned

fixed: Changed 'so that I may be burned' to 'to be burned' to match the passive sense of the Greek subjunctive καυθήσωμαι and the standard rendering of 1 Corinthians 13:3, where Paul speaks of surrendering his body to be burned by others, not of self-immolation.

last_rejected.why: Paul says 'I am benefited nothing,' not 'I gain nothing'—the verb is about benefit, not gain.
last_rejected.ruling: ὠφελοῦμαι means 'I am benefited/profited'; 'gain' is within normal range, not misleading.

last_rejected.why: Source has no explicit subject; 'Paul' is an editorial addition not in Greek.
last_rejected.ruling: Context makes Paul the subject; supplying it is standard interpretive rendering, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.fix: he did not fully perceive those good things until he saw his brothers being saved with him
last_rejected.ruling: εἰ μὴ regularly means 'unless'; rendering as conditional is within normal Greek usage.

last_rejected.fix: the crown and sum of all good things
last_rejected.ruling: κεφάλαιον as 'chief point, principal thing' is standard LSJ range; not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: Κυρώσατε means 'confirm, ratify, make firm' not 'reaffirm'; this is a technical term for official confirmation.
last_rejected.ruling: Reaffirm is within normal range of κυρόω; no meaning lost or changed.
